name: Strategy & strategy statement
purpose: What is strategy, and what must a strategy statement say?

parts.label: Definition
points: Strategy = the long-term direction (trajectory) of an organization
Three words: long-term · direction · organization

parts.label: Why – purpose
points: Mission and vision (expected future to create)
Values (moral principles)
Objectives (outcomes to achieve)

parts.label: Where – industry & scope → corporate strategy
points: Customer segments
Geography
Activities (vertical integration)

parts.label: How – resources & capabilities → business strategy
points: How the organization competes with what it has and does

apply: Reconstruct the firm's Why / Where / How from the case
Check consistency: does the How support the Where and the Why?
example: L'Oréal (CEO interview 2025): strengths in Beauty Tech & AI, sustainability, culture; investments in R&I (> €1.3bn), emerging markets, Gen Z, men, boomers; goal: reach 2bn consumers.

name: Levels of strategy
purpose: At which level is a strategic decision taken?

parts.label: Corporate strategy
points: Scope of the organization
Geographical scope, diversification, resource allocation to businesses

parts.label: Business strategy
points: How businesses compete in their markets
Innovation, scale, response to competition

parts.label: Functional strategies
points: How the components (marketing, operations, HR …) implement corporate and business strategy

parts.label: Strategic integration
points: The three levels must fit together

apply: Classify the question: “where to compete?” = corporate, “how to compete?” = business

name: What is strategy?
purpose: Why is operational effectiveness not enough, and what makes a strategy sustainable?

parts.label: Operational effectiveness ≠ strategy
points: OE = same activities done better (productivity frontier)
Best practices diffuse → competitive convergence

parts.label: Unique position
points: Variety-based (subset of products, Jiffy Lube)
Needs-based (most needs of one group, IKEA)
Access-based (customers reachable differently, rural cinemas)

parts.label: Trade-offs
points: Choose what NOT to do
Protect against straddlers (Continental Lite vs Southwest)

parts.label: Fit among activities
points: 1st order: consistency
2nd order: activities reinforce each other
3rd order: optimization of effort
The whole system is hard to imitate

apply: Name what the firm does differently (activities), not just better
Check whether a new move fits or blurs the activity system (growth trap)
pitfalls: Ignoring the growth trap: broadening the line blurs the position

name: Five Ps for strategy
purpose: In which different senses can we speak of a strategy?

parts.label: Plan
points: Consciously intended course of action, set in advance

parts.label: Ploy
points: A manoeuvre to outwit an opponent

parts.label: Pattern
points: Consistency in behaviour over time, intended or not

parts.label: Position
points: Location in the environment: niche, product-market domain

parts.label: Perspective
points: Shared way of seeing the world – the “personality”; hardest to change

parts.label: Deliberate vs emergent
points: Intended & realized = deliberate
Intended, not realized = unrealized
Realized without intention = emergent (Honda in the US)

apply: Ask whether the firm's strategy was planned or emerged from practice
Check whether a new position is compatible with the perspective

name: Why organizations matter
purpose: Why do organizations (and their boundaries) matter for strategy?

parts.label: Chandler – The Visible Hand
points: Railroads & telegraph → markets could not coordinate the volumes
Advantage = throughput, not size
Investments: large plants, national distribution, management hierarchy
Structure follows strategy (multidivisional form)

parts.label: Perrow – A Society of Organizations
points: Organizations absorbed society
Kept gains, pushed costs onto workers, communities, the state
Alternative: networks of small specialized firms

parts.label: Simon – Organizations and Markets
points: Martian view: green areas (organizations), thin red lines (markets)
Authority, rewards, identification, coordination

parts.label: So what
points: Firm boundaries (internalize vs outsource) are strategic choices with economic and social consequences

name: Explaining organizational performance
purpose: Why are some organizations more successful than others – and why is that hard to answer?

parts.label: Competitive advantage
points: Persistently higher profit (or potential) than rivals in the same market
Sources: cost structure, quality, branding …

parts.label: Four challenges
points: Relevant factors are hard to identify
Causality is hard to establish (endogeneity)
Performance is multi-dimensional (economic, social …)
Will the model hold over time and across places?

pitfalls: Measuring every organization by profit only (clubs, parties, churches, universities)
example: Performance of PSG, Goldman Sachs, ESCP, US parties, Tesla, the Church, Le Monde, TikTok is measured very differently.
